checkpoints.description: Task 'review-findings-remediation-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] ui finish: when review is the only blocker, say so and drop the revert/allow/abort advice; exit code and the ui.review-missing JSON code unchanged. [2/3] check_reachability: delete the dead all_literals fallback, correct its comment to the strict behaviour, and pin with a regression test that a producer hidden in a comprehension is flagged. [3/3] Ledger version: accept 1 <= version <= current on both read and write, still refusing < 1, newer and non-int; align data_models.md; ADR-178 recording the 27-ledger correction to ADR-174.

impact_assessment.why: Three findings reproduced end to end. ui finish tells a user whose change verify just passed that it is outside its contract and leads with abort, which reverts the work. The reachability fallback is dead because a set cannot count above 1, and its comment describes a weaker behaviour that would have passed a hidden producer this session. validate_ledger_version and save_ledger refuse every version but the current one, so the first schema bump makes all 27 v1 ledgers unreadable and migrate_ledger_schema can never run.
impact_assessment.benefits: A user blocked only on review is told exactly that and keeps their work; the safety gate keeps its strict behaviour without a comment inviting someone to weaken it; a future schema bump can migrate existing ledgers instead of stopping every ledger command across 27 ledgers.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: finish's human stderr text changes in the review-only case, exit code 1 and JSON codes unchanged; the ledger accepts older valid versions, but with LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION 1 that is identical to today. dependency: none. concurrency: none. state: no ledger is rewritten; acceptance widens only below the current version and all existing refusals (True, '2', 2.0, 0, -1, newer) stay.
impact_assessment.mitigation: A failing-first test per milestone; reproduce the finish message against a real sandbox project; keep test_invalid_ledger_versions_are_refused unchanged and green; change both version checks through one shared predicate so they cannot drift; commit each milestone separately after its Phase 4 passes, per PRINCIPLE-006 R1.

checkpoints.description: Task 'three-findings-fix-v1' completed successfully.

[1/1] Raise the --help cold-start budget from 200ms to 250ms by user decision: dogfood.py budget_ms and its stale ADR-083 comment, PRINCIPLE-010's capsule and R5 text, the README matrix row, the P-010 rule-text pin test; leave R2's unrelated 200ms concurrency threshold untouched; regenerate all 8 targets; ADR-179 with P-010's cross-principle check; measure the residual flake rate at 250ms; run every Phase 4 gate.

impact_assessment.why: The user decided to raise the limit. dogfood times aikit.py --help once against 200ms, and on this machine aikit.py has a ~160ms floor because it imports nearly every module to print help, so ordinary Windows process-start jitter exceeded 200ms in about 16 percent of samples and failed 2 of 4 full Phase 4 sequences plus one isolated verify_commit run.
impact_assessment.benefits: Phase 4 and verify_commit stop failing on startup-time jitter that no code change caused, so a red gate again means a real defect rather than an unlucky sample.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: PRINCIPLE-010's stated --help budget and every document that repeats it change from 200ms to 250ms; R2's separate 200ms threading threshold must not change. dependency: none. concurrency: none. state: no persisted data; the capsule changes length by zero characters, so the Tier 1 budget is unaffected.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Change only the --help occurrences, verified by grep; keep TestRuleNumberParity tying dogfood's constant to the rule text; name the edited pin test in ADR-179 so the change is visible; record in ADR-179 that the user chose this over best-of-N measurement and lazy imports, and that the underlying ~160ms floor is unchanged; measure and state the residual failure rate at 250ms.
